message: Published IWM research using the linked public evidence. The futures reporting dates are shown in the analysis; refreshing this page does not generate a new report.

data.headline: IWM: less net short, but no broad agreement.
data.summary: Russell E-mini futures show two different changes in the October 27 report. Leveraged funds were less net short, while asset managers held a smaller net long balance. That combination does not establish broad demand for IWM or a small-cap reversal.

bull.text: Leveraged funds’ Russell E-mini net short balance narrowed from 53,035 contracts on October 20 to 48,081 on October 27, a reduction of 4,954. Both gross longs and gross shorts declined, so the net improvement should not be described as fresh long buying.

bear.text: Asset managers’ net long balance declined from 30,960 to 19,602 contracts across the same dates. Long positions fell from 148,470 to 142,993 while short positions rose from 117,510 to 123,391.

watch.text: Open interest declined from 466,789 to 458,959 contracts. Look for whether the next report changes both gross exposure and the split between categories; contract counts do not measure dollars entering or leaving IWM.

limitations: CFTC observations are for October 27 and October 20, 2026. These are weekly futures-only reports released after their observation dates, not live positions.
The related futures contract is not the ETF. Trader-category net positions are long-minus-short contract counts; they are not ETF fund flows, dollar exposure or evidence of investor intent.
No current support/resistance levels, options chain, gamma levels or dark-pool signal were collected for this report. Hosted charts remain separate from the editorial evidence.
This AI-assisted report presents supporting observations and counterpoints, without a validated price forecast or conviction score. It is general research, not a buy or sell instruction.
